items.heading: Explains the matter of coupling by striking, of the observation of the eyes in AHP [Ozen-Hotem-Peh], from which the vessels came about, with additional explanation. —
items.html: *A discourse that I wrote concerning the matter of the roots of Atzilut, of the self and vessels that came about from AHP [Ozen-Hotem-Peh, ear-nose-mouth] and the eyes, in the secret of sight, hearing, smell, and speech. This I found in the name of Rabbi Gedalia HaLevi. When the lights expanded from the ear and the nose to opposite the mouth, where all the breaths join together, then in the place where they join, all of them have the phase of Nefesh. For the breath of the ear cannot join with the breath of the mouth except at a distance of place. And likewise the breath of the nose, except that it does not need as great a distance of place as the breath of the ear in order to join with the breath of the mouth. And for this the observation of the eyes comes, and by the striking that it struck in this breath, the vessels were made. And in this observation there is internal and external, for in every organ there is internality and externality, and the totality of their vessels was made. And since in the sight of the eyes there is no breath that goes out, but observation alone, only vessels are made by it, not more.

This observation is greater than all three of the aforementioned breaths, for sight is Yod, hearing is Heh, smell is Vav, speech is Heh — thus the four letters of HaVaYaH, which are Hochma-Bina-Tifferet-Malchut [Chabad-Tum], which are Neshama-Ruach-Nefesh-Chaya [NaRaNCh]: sight is the Yod of Chaya of the name, which is called Hochma. For the upper Hochma shines by way of the eyes, but if breath actually went out through the eyes, it would not be possible for the lower ones to receive it; therefore only observation alone is extended from it, and it had the power to make vessels for these three phases: the Yod of Neshama in the breath of the ear, the Yod of Ruach in the breath of the nose, the Yod of Nefesh in the breath of the mouth. And this is the secret of “from afar the Lord appeared to me.” And of the other breaths, had observation alone come from them through a screen as with the eyes, they would have had no power to make vessels. And all this holds both for the phase of the expansion of the breath and for the observation of sight. And this sight is numerically equal to Gevura, and speech is numerically equal to two hundred sixteen with the four letters.

And this observation comes and strikes at the place where the three breaths join together, which is the phase of Nefesh, and this is “and Elokim saw the light,” for the light is the phase of the breath of the ear and the nose, which is the phase of Neshama and Ruach. The darkness is the phase of the mouth, which is Nefesh. And then, when He saw the Nefesh, then “and Elokim separated,” which is the making of the roots of the vessels.

And this observation, in the direct way, made an imprint (another version: heads) in each and every phase. For it met, in each and every phase, from the observation: for the phase of the breath of Keter, in Keter. And in like manner every imprint (another version: beginning) of the vessels was made, the external ones in the external organs, and the internal ones in the internal organs, and this was not completed until the observation struck in the place where the breaths join, which is the expansion of the breaths, which is their externality; and from the striking of the light of the breath against the light of the observation, the light of the observation returned by way of reflected light, and a vessel was made in every phase for the rest of the body: the external ones for the external organs, and the internal ones for the internal organs.

1And since, in observation, whatever is more attached to its root is more upper, 2for Keter (another version: the Keter), which is adjacent to the eye, came out last, and Malchut came out first, 3and when it strikes and returns, then every phase of the vessels is equal: 4for if Yesod had expanded inward more than Malchut (it would have been equal to Malchut) it is because of Malchut (even though it is Yesod that expanded more), for Yesod, from the abundance of light (upon) Malchut, had the power to expand further, 5and it has no advantage over Malchut, but rather because this expansion is in the secret of reflected light, which returns and draws near to its source; but in the phase of the vessels themselves, they are equal.

And when the light returns and clothes the breath, it is found that, when it is adjacent to the mouth, the breath of the mouth is greater than the breath of the ear, for the breath of the mouth is now adjacent to the mouth in the phase of Rosh, while the breath of the ear is still in the phase of the rest of the body, until it rises opposite the ear.
